paragraphs: Friend, here's what I see in this one. Saul is scared, and he goes looking for an answer. The LORD did not answer him by dreams or Urim or prophets (1 Samuel 28:6), so Saul went to a medium at Endor, even though he had removed the mediums and spiritists from the land (1 Samuel 28:3, 7). When the answer you want doesn't come, it's tempting to go shopping for a different one, and I've been in a dark drawer long enough to understand that feeling.

Now look at what Saul got for his trouble. Samuel asks him, "Why do you consult me, since the LORD has turned away from you and become your enemy?" (1 Samuel 28:16). Samuel says the LORD did this because Saul did not obey Him or carry out His burning anger against Amalek (1 Samuel 28:18), and then he adds that tomorrow Saul and his sons will be with him (1 Samuel 28:19). Going another way didn't undo what the LORD had spoken, and it left Saul terrified by the words of Samuel (1 Samuel 28:20).

So here's what I want you to carry out of my bakery, baker. When you're scared, go to the LORD, and keep listening to what He has already said. His Word is the one place you can count on to be true. Saul chased a shortcut, and a shortcut to the wrong place is still a long way from home. And this story isn't over, so keep that apron on.
